text_blocks.snippet: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) occurs when blood vessels in the lungs become narrowed, blocked, or destroyed, forcing the right side of the heart to work harder to pump blood.
snippet_highlighted_words: blood vessels in the lungs become narrowed, blocked, or destroyed

text_blocks.snippet: In the early stages, PAH often causes no noticeable symptoms. As the condition progresses, signs develop that frequently mimic other heart or lung illnesses.

list.snippet: Shortness of breath (dyspnea), especially during routine physical activity like climbing stairs or walking
Fatigue and general weakness from reduced oxygen flow
Chest pain or pressure from an overworked, strained heart
Heart palpitations or a racing, pounding heartbeat

text_blocks.snippet: Advanced Symptoms (Indicating Increased Heart Strain or Failure)

list.snippet: Swelling (edema) in the ankles, legs, feet, or abdomen due to fluid retention
Fainting spells (syncope), particularly during or right after exertion
Bluish lips or skin (cyanosis) caused by low oxygen levels
Coughing up blood (hemoptysis) in severe cases

text_blocks.snippet: You can learn more about recognizing and testing for these signs through the American Lung Association or the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

list.snippet: Which specific symptoms are happening and how long they have lasted
